transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well... I guess what scared me enough to actually come in today is that I just keep thinking it would be a relief if I didn't wake up in the morning. I mean, I haven't tried to hurt myself or do anything like that. But just having those thoughts... it really frightened me.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up?
Well, I'd say it's been going on for about four months now. It started right around the time my aunt came to live with us.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do over the past four months?

No, not really. I used to look forward to doing my watercolors, going to my dance class, and taking walks with the ladies in the neighborhood. But lately... I just leave my paints sitting there. I can't even make myself care enough to go out and do any of it anymore.
Do you still find pleasure in the things you're doing, even if you're not doing as many of them as you used to?

No, not at all. Like I was just saying... I really just can't make myself care anymore. Even if I were to force myself to sit down with my watercolors, I don't get any joy out of it. It's why I just leave my things sitting there now. That good feeling I used to get from painting, or my dance class, or being out with the ladies... it's just completely gone.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how quickly you move compared to before these thoughts started?

Well, my husband says I move like everything takes extra effort now. I guess I've noticed it too... even when I go to the market, I just stand there for too long before I pick up what I came for. It just feels like I'm moving slower.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight since these thoughts started?
No, I haven't really noticed any change there. My clothes still fit about the same as they always have, so... no, I don't think my weight has gone up or down.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty about anything lately?

Well... yes, I have. My aunt lives with us, and sometimes I just get so tired or annoyed with her. But then... I start thinking I'm a terrible woman for feeling that way. I just feel like I'm bringing shame on my whole family because I can't be more grateful for what I have. It just makes me feel awful about myself.
Have you been having these thoughts about not waking up every day, or are there some days when you don't think about it at all?

It's... well, it's pretty much every day lately. Honestly, that's what scared me enough to actually come in here and see you. I just keep thinking it would be such a relief if I just didn't wake up in the morning. I haven't tried to hurt myself or do anything like that, but... I do have that thought a lot.
Have you had any days in the past week where you didn't feel this way at all?
No, I don't think so. It's... it's been pretty constant this whole past week. I haven't really had a day where I didn't feel that way, no.
Have you had any difficulty concentrating or making decisions over the past four months?

No, not really. I haven't noticed any trouble with that. I mean, I can still focus on things and... make decisions just fine. It's really just the other feelings I mentioned. My mind is still pretty clear when it comes to paying attention to things, so no, that hasn't been an issue.
Would you say these thoughts of not wanting to wake up and your lack of enjoyment in activities are interfering with your daily life a lot, or just somewhat?

I'd say a lot. I've completely stopped going to my dance class and my walking group. I also usually help out at the food pantry, but I've been missing my shifts there, too. Even just around the house, my husband has had to take over doing more of the errands because I just... I get stuck and fall behind on things. So, yes, it's interfering quite a bit.
Would you say these thoughts and feelings have been present most of the day, nearly every day, over the past four months?
Yes, most of the day, nearly every day. It's been going on for about four months now... ever since my aunt came to live with us. That's when it all started.
Would you say these thoughts and feelings have caused you significant distress or impairment in your social, occupational, or other areas of functioning?

Yes, very much so. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it's really getting in the way of my normal life. I've completely stopped going to my dance class and the walking group, and I'm missing my shifts at the food pantry. And... well, at home I just get stuck and fall behind on things, so my husband has had to take over doing most of the errands. So, yes, it's definitely causing a lot of problems for me.
Would you say these feelings of not wanting to wake up and your lack of enjoyment in activities are extremely severe, or more moderate?
I wouldn't say they're extremely severe, no. Maybe more mild to moderate. It's just... a constant heavy feeling, but it's not the worst it could possibly be, I suppose.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety lately?

No, not restless. Actually, it's more the opposite. My husband says I move like everything takes extra effort now. Even when I do manage to go to the market, I just... I stand there too long before picking up what I came for. It's like I'm moving in slow motion.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

No, not really. I used to really look forward to painting with my watercolors, and like I said, the dance class and walking with the ladies... but lately, I just leave my paints sitting out. I can't even make myself pick up the brush. I just... I can't make myself care about any of it anymore.
Would you say your feelings of sadness or depression are present most of the day?

Yes, I'd say so. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy sadness right in my chest. It's just... it's like I've already failed the day before it even starts. And that feeling pretty much stays with me until I go back to sleep.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find pleasure in?

Well, like I was saying just a minute ago... it's mostly just the watercolor painting, the dance class, and walking with the ladies. I can't really think of anything else besides those. I just don't have the interest for them right now.
Would you say your feelings of sadness or depression have been interfering with your ability to work or take care of things at home most days?

Yes, it definitely has. I've stopped going to my dance class and the walking group, like I mentioned, but I've also stopped showing up for my shifts at the food pantry. I just can't get myself out the door. At home... well, my husband has had to take over a lot more of the errands. I just get stuck, you know? I can't seem to get moving, and I just fall behind on everything I'm supposed to be doing.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Not really, no. Like I was saying about my watercolors and the dance class and walking with the ladies... I used to really look forward to those. But lately, I just leave my things sitting there. I look at my paints and I just can't make myself care. So, no, there isn't really anything I'm enjoying right now.
